ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, element A is drawn as a rectangle, with two terminals above and below; the reference polarity of voltage U is marked on the left side, with the upper terminal as “+” and the lower terminal as “-”. The reference arrow of current I is on the upper branch, with its direction pointing toward element A, that is, the current reference direction enters the positive terminal of the voltage. Given by the problem U = 220 V, I = -1 A. Since the current reference direction in the figure enters the positive terminal, it conforms to the passive sign convention, so the power absorbed by the element is calculated according to P = U I. Substituting gives P = 220 × (-1) = -220 W.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: U is measured with + at the top terminal and - at the bottom terminal, while I is referenced as entering the top terminal of A. From the text, I = -1 A, so the actual current is 1 A opposite the arrow, leaving the positive terminal. A device with current leaving its positive terminal is delivering power, not consuming it. The power magnitude is 220 V × 1 A = 220 W, so the consumed power is P = -220 W.
